newsitem.title: USA: Orange County D.A. recommends sentence for Citron.
newsitem.headline: Orange County D.A. recommends sentence for Citron.

text.p: The former treasurer of California's Orange County should serve seven years in state prison for crimes stemming from the largest municipal bankruptcy in the nation's history, the county District Attorney said on Tuesday.
In court papers filed in Santa Ana, Orange County District Attorney Michael Capizzi also recommended that former Treasurer Robert Citron be fined $400,000.

In a separate filing, Citron attorney David Wiechert urged the court to sentence Citron to probation and fine him $10,000. If any confinement were to be required, Citron should only receive home detention, Wiechert argued.
A probation report prepared for the court recommended that Citron receive a year or less in county jail and probation.
Citron pleaded guilty last year to several counts of securities fraud and misappropriation of public funds. He faces up to 14 years in prison.
The court will review the recommendations. A sentencing hearing has been set for November 18.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on December 6, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June 1996.
